title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints for Quantum Channels: A Spacetime-Duality View
authors: Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Yu-Jie Liu, Tsung-Cheng Lu, Frank Pollmann, Yizhi You
abstract: Quantum anomalies strongly constrain the possible behavior of many-body systems. A prime example is the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem, which relates UV symmetry and filling constraints to IR features of the energy spectrum and ground-state structure. Here, we ask how LSM constraints shape dynamical signatures and temporal correlations in open quantum systems. Using a spacetime duality, we show that the Liouvillian of a $d$-dimensional repeated quantum channel with a mixed anomaly between strong $S$ and weak $G$ symmetry can be mapped to a $(d{+}1)$-dimensional mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (mSPT) phase. Under this correspondence, the initial and steady states of the channel are identified with boundary states of the higher-dimensional mSPT in the presence of bulk projection. We further introduce the twisted Renyi-$N$ correlator (TRNC) as a probe of temporal correlations in the channel and demonstrate that it is dual to the mSPT strange correlator, providing a direct bulk-boundary route to diagnose long-range temporal order implied by the LSM anomaly. Finally, we identify the \textit{Liouvillian singular spectrum}, rather than the Liouvillian spectrum itself, as a more fundamental diagnostic of quantum anomalies, and show that it is dual to the operator entanglement spectrum of the mSPT.
summary: This paper extends the Lieb-Schultz-Mattis theorem to open quantum systems by analyzing the dynamics governed by quantum channels. Using a spacetime duality, the authors map the time evolution to a higher-dimensional mixed-state topological phase. This allows them to diagnose long-range temporal order, implied by LSM anomalies, by studying dual spatial correlators.
main_problem: The paper investigates how Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) constraints, typically for ground states, dictate the dynamical signatures and temporal correlations in open quantum systems.
main_result: The authors establish a spacetime duality mapping the dynamics of a quantum channel to a higher-dimensional mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (mSPT) phase, providing a bulk-boundary diagnostic for LSM anomalies.
method: The core method involves using spacetime duality to map the time evolution governed by a quantum channel's Liouvillian to a spatial correlation problem in a dual mSPT phase.
model_or_system: The system under study is an open quantum system undergoing Markovian dynamics, modeled by repeated application of a quantum channel $E$. The analysis uses the Liouvillian formalism on a doubled Hilbert space.
key_observables: Twisted Rényi-N correlator (TRNC), Liouvillian singular spectrum, and the operator entanglement spectrum of the dual mSPT.
important_parameters: The dimensionality $d$ of the channel, and the nature of the mixed anomaly between strong $S$ and weak $G$ symmetries.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies fundamentally on the spacetime duality correspondence between the channel dynamics and the mSPT phase.
paper_structure: The paper first extends the LSM theorem to open systems, then uses the Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism to map the channel to a transfer matrix $Q$. It then employs spacetime duality to map the temporal evolution to a higher-dimensional mSPT, defining the TRNC and relating it to the mSPT strange correlator.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general framework connecting fundamental theorems from condensed matter (LSM) to the non-equilibrium dynamics of open quantum systems using advanced topological concepts (mSPT).
